items.title: Rheologically tuned diffusion modulates quorum sensing in Vibrio fischeri
items.summary: Understanding how the physical properties of a fluid influence bacterial behavior is essential for explaining how microorganisms interact with their environment and with animal hosts. Here, we examine how changes in fluid viscosity and rheological properties affect the locomotion of the marine bacterium Vibrio fischeri and its ability to produce luminescence through cell--cell communication. We track the three-dimensional motion of single cells in well-defined fluids with different physical properties and measure the luminescence emitted by cell populations. We find that fluids with higher viscosity cause V. fischeri to spend more time in a slower, turning-focused swimming mode, which reduces how effectively cells spread out and encounter the chemical signals required to activate luminescence. As a result, luminescence first increases and then decreases in Newtonian fluids, but decreases monotonically in fluids that exhibit non-Newtonian rheological behavior. Computer simulations based on our measurements confirm that the ability of cells to explore their surroundings plays a central role in determining when and how strongly they communicate. These findings reveal a direct link between the physical environment, bacterial movement, and collective behavior, and offer insight into how microorganisms adapt to complex fluid habitats, including those found inside animal hosts.

items.title: Symmetry-Guided Machine Learning of Spin-Dependent Nonlinear Hall Response
items.summary: A Berry-curvature dipole can generate a current perpendicular to an applied electric field even when the linear Hall response is zero. This work examines how lattice symmetry, magnetic orientation, and carrier occupation control this nonlinear response in an anisotropic honeycomb model. Unequal hopping permits one dipole component without magnetism. Rotating the local moments can activate the second component and change the sign and magnitude of both. Reversing all moments leaves the dipole unchanged but reverses the intrinsic linear Hall conductivity. Equal populations of reversed domains can therefore retain the dipole contribution when their local electric fields are the same. A symmetry-constrained polynomial machine-learning model describes the calculated dipoles for 1024 spin configurations. At the reference chemical potential, both components have $R^2>0.9995$ for 256 configurations excluded from training. Keeping the carrier density fixed shifts the chemical potential as the moments rotate and gives slightly larger prediction errors. Separate fits across a chemical-potential sweep show a stronger loss of accuracy for $D_y$ at higher energies. Within weak-field semiclassical transport with a constant relaxation time, the predicted dipole determines the angular dependence, rectification, and second harmonic of the current. The results connect magnetic control of the nonlinear Hall response to the balance of Berry-curvature contributions near the Fermi level.

items.title: Aging and protocol dependence of thermal activation events in structural glasses
items.summary: In this study, we investigate the waiting time dependence and the protocol dependence of thermally activated events in structural glasses using molecular simulations and potential energy landscape analysis. We find a qualitative crossover in the nature of activation events; from avalanche-like events to local events. We also use the isoconfigurational ensemble analysis and reveal that the events become less diverse and more reversible. We discuss these crossovers from the perspective of the stability and the potential energy landscape of glasses. To investigate the protocol dependence, we compare the two types of glasses whose stability is controlled by waiting time and parent temperature, respectively. Surprisingly, at the same inherent structure energy level, the parent-temperature-controlled glasses are more unstable and maintain their avalanche-like nature. These results demonstrate that the activation properties of structural glasses are not determined solely by their energy levels, highlighting the essential role of state connectivity and the dynamical sampling in the complex energy landscape.

items.title: Single-stripe magnetic order and bilayer spin dynamics in single-crystalline La3Ni2O7
items.summary: High-temperature superconductivity in pressurized and thin-film nickelates has generated intense interest, yet magnetism in their ambient-pressure parent phases remains poorly understood, despite its potentially crucial role in pairing. Progress has been limited by the lack of large single crystals suitable for neutron spectroscopy. Here we overcome this limitation and map the spin order and excitations of single-crystalline La3Ni2O7. We find single-stripe magnetic order with a finite spin gap, anisotropic in-plane excitations and pronounced bilayer modulation revealing antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling. The dispersion is captured by a bilayer Heisenberg-type model with strong interlayer exchange and competing in-plane couplings. Absolute normalization reveals that, although the spin-wave bandwidth is only about 25% of that in cuprates, the local dynamic susceptibility at comparable energies is enhanced, yielding a comparable total fluctuating moment. These results highlight intense mid-energy spin excitations rooted in substantial electronic correlations, establishing a magnetic framework distinct from cuprates and relevant to superconductivity in nickelates.

items.title: Solving fractional quantum Hall problems with thermodynamic-limit bootstrap
items.summary: Determining correlated ground states directly in the thermodynamic limit remains a central challenge in quantum many-body physics. Here we develop a quantum many-body bootstrap that yields a rigorous and tight lower bound on the thermodynamic ground-state energy of a fractional quantum Hall system together with an optimized reduced density matrix $ρ_W^\star$ on a spatial window. For sufficiently tight bounds, we find that $ρ_W^\star$ accurately reproduces the ground-state reduced density matrix, as directly tested by its fidelity with known model states. For exactly solvable Laughlin and Moore--Read parent Hamiltonians, the bootstrap also reproduces pair correlations and orbital entanglement spectra (OES). For Landau-level-projected Coulomb interactions across multiple fillings, the energy bounds closely track established thermodynamic estimates, while the window density matrix recovers the familiar $ν=1/3$ Laughlin and $ν=5/2$ Moore--Read states and the composite Fermi liquid at $ν=1/2$. More importantly, the same framework also resolves unsettled regimes. At $ν=1/4$, the OES and real-space correlations identify a composite Fermi liquid, while at $ν=12/5$ the combined diagnostics suggest $\overline{\mathrm{RR}}_3$ as the ground-state order. Our bootstrap therefore provides direct access to both ground-state energies and many-body structure in the thermodynamic limit.

items.title: Metastability, collective excitations, and traveling states of one-dimensional spin-orbit-coupled quantum droplets
items.summary: We study the static and traveling droplet phases of spin-orbit coupled, one-dimensional Bose-Bose mixtures with a Lee-Huang-Yang correction. For the static droplets, employing a variational analysis for an infinitely extended mixture, we show that the system can feature two ground-state droplet phases: a stripe droplet phase up to a critical Rabi coupling strength, at which it undergoes a first-order transition to a zero-momentum droplet phase. The variational results for the ground-state properties are shown to be in good agreement with numerical solutions for droplets in the thermodynamic limit as well as finite-size droplets in the "flat-top regime". For finite-size droplets, the stripe phase can feature multiple stationary states with different numbers of peaks in their stripe density patterns. The calculation of the excitation spectrum for these stationary states confirms their stability. To study the moving droplets, we investigate the ground-state phases of the system in the droplet's comoving frame. We show that in the comoving frame, droplets acquire a finite longitudinal magnetization. As a consequence, the phase diagram features two distinct phases: a traveling stripe droplet and a plane-wave droplet. The real-time evolution of these droplets in the space-fixed frame, complemented by the Bogoliubov analysis in the comoving frame, illustrates the stability of these traveling droplet phases.

items.title: A Zoo of Fermionic Relative Rényi Negativities in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Models
items.summary: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource that gives rise to correlations with no classical counterpart in strongly correlated fermionic systems. However, its characterization in mixed quantum states remains challenging. Established entanglement diagnostics, such as logarithmic negativity, are computationally demanding in interacting systems, and their evaluation by exact diagonalization is restricted to small system sizes. Meanwhile, conventional Rényi proxies, including twisted and untwisted Rényi negativities, can be positive even for separable states. In this work, we introduce a family of \textit{relative Rényi negativities} that serve as entanglement witnesses. By relating fermionic partial time reversal to the size superoperator, we establish a path-integral representation for these Rényi negativities, enabling their evaluation in thermal states of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model and its generalizations via a large-$N$ expansion. Applying this method, we investigate entanglement in both the original SYK model and the Maldacena-Qi coupled SYK model. We identify a special class of relative Rényi negativities which serve as plausible proxies for logarithmic negativity and uncover first-order entanglement transitions that are invisible to simple observables. These results highlight the utility of relative Rényi negativities as probes of mixed-state entanglement in strongly correlated fermionic systems and suggest the existence of a new class of transitions where these negativities serve as free energies.

items.title: Position- and Temperature-Dependent Responsivity in a KID-Based Phonon-Mediated Detector
items.summary: We report on the position- and temperature-dependent response of a kinetic inductance phonon-mediated (KIPM) detector. To study position-dependence, we used a controllable mirror attached to a micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) to steer optical light with a 100 $μ$m spot size over the backside of the cryogenic detector. With both pulsed and continuous operation of the LED, we observe features of the detector housing and find that the signal is strongest when the LED is pointed directly at the KID. The "off-KID" response is measured to be 34% of the "on-KID" response and is largely independent of direction. We model phonon propagation and collection in the KIPM detector with G4CMP and assert that the isotropic angular dependence is unlikely to be due to discrete phonon absorption "sinks", such as the microwave feedline or the device mounting points, but can be explained instead by an isotropic energy loss in the crystal. We furthermore utilize the temperature flexibility of the MEMS and KIPM detector system to investigate temperature-dependent responsivity, both at the sensor level (i.e., frequency shifts in the KID) and at the detector level (i.e., position dependence). We fit the KID's response to a two-component heat capacity and present the model as an alternative way to understand the KID's response to absorbed energy. We show on- and off-KID data at a range of temperatures and show that the phonon dynamics are not temperature dependent. We comment on the resulting implication for KID dynamics and design improvements.

items.title: Ten-loop fixed-dimension renormalization-group functions of the three-dimensional O(N) model from distributed GPU-accelerated parametric integration
items.summary: The renormalization-group functions $β$, $η$ and $ν$ of the three-dimensional $O(N)$ model in fixed dimension (massive zero-momentum scheme) were known to eighth order in the coupling. We extend them to tenth order, and $β$ to eleventh, for general $N$, which requires the two- and four-point functions to ten loops (1,593,254 graphs at the last order), and re-evaluate all lower orders. Through the Callan-Symanzik equation every coefficient follows from per-order sums that are linear in finite, zero-momentum $\bar R$-subtracted parametric integrals, one per graph, which we sample on GPUs by tropical Monte Carlo with densities adapted to the forest terms. The computation reproduces the known sums from two to seven loops within three standard deviations and agrees at ninth and tenth order, at lower precision, with an independent route through an intermediate scheme. The new coefficients have relative uncertainties of a few $10^{-5}$ or better, and the eighth-order coefficients of $η$ and $ν$ improve by factors of 120 and 4. The time needed to integrate an order to fixed relative precision grows by only 2.4-2.9 per loop from seven loops on, while the construction of the integrands still grows factorially and, at tenth order, costs more than the integration. Resummed, the tenth-order series give $ν=0.62997(51)$, $η=0.0333(18)$ and $ω=0.803(14)$ for $N=1$, against $0.62997097(12)$, $0.036297612(48)$ and $0.82968(23)$ from the conformal bootstrap; at $N=3$ the deviations grow, so that the uncertainty is now dominated by the resummation rather than by the coefficients. Every result is generated automatically from, or checked against, a public ledger of independent, exactly pooled runs, hosted on GitHub, to which anyone is welcome to contribute computing time.

items.title: Th$^{4+}$ ion cluster structures and electric field gradients in $^{229}$Th:CaF$_2$
items.summary: The low-energy nuclear isomeric transition of $^{229}$Th is a promising frequency reference for a solid-state nuclear optical clock. Wide-band-gap fluoride crystals such as CaF$_2$ offer transparent hosts for embedding Th nuclei at high density. Substitution of Th$^{4+}$ for Ca$^{2+}$ requires charge compensation, linking the local defect structure to nuclear quadrupole splitting. We use first-principles calculations to examine neutral Th dimers compensated by four interstitial F ions ($\mathrm{F}_{i}^{-}$). Screening different compensation geometries by their relative formation energies identifies a family of low-energy configurations with closely similar local structures. These configurations share large electric field gradients and small asymmetry parameters, consistent with the experimental high-EFG site 3. Their calculated quadrupole splittings are further compared with the measured C13 spectra. Together, the energetic and spectroscopic results support $\mathrm{F}_{i}^{-}$-compensated Th dimers as candidate microscopic structures for site 3 in Th:CaF$_2$.

items.title: Scaling Dimensions and Two-Point Amplitudes from Operator Covariance Matrices
items.summary: The long distance behavior of two-point functions of critical lattice statistical mechanics models depend on detailed information of the underlying quantum field theory. Yet these universal properties can be difficult to extract because generic lattice operators couple to the infinite hierarchy of continuum scaling operators with unknown coefficients. Recently in Physical Review E 114, 024146 (2026), one approach to disentangle some of this information was proposed using the eigen-decomposition of the operator covariance matrix constructed from cross correlations of a finite set of $N_\ell$ lattice operators. In this work we analyze this method in detail. We provide an explicit proof that under the assumption of scale invariance the leading decay of the eigenvalues are controlled by the smallest $N_\ell$ scaling dimensions, even after taking irrelevant perturbations into account. Based on this understanding, we propose a new method by which the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix can be used to construct the amplitudes of the continuum two-point correlation functions. This allows for a complete determination of the structure of the continuum two-point functions from the lattice covariance matrix. We demonstrate our ideas both on synthetic data sets (drawn from the scaling hypothesis) and numerically exact data for the two dimensional Ising model.

items.title: Dissipation dilution enhances SiV coupling to vdW diamond nanomechanics
items.summary: Solid-state color centers embedded into mechanical resonators, where orbital states mediate interactions between spins and long-lived phonons, are a promising platform for hybrid quantum systems. The negatively charged silicon vacancy center in diamond (SiV-) is particularly favorable for strain-coupling to nanomechanical resonators because of its large spin-strain susceptibility and compatibility with device integration. Tensioned nanomechanical resonators offer an attractive route due to their ultra-long mechanical coherence times enabled by diluting defect-induced dissipation, though it is unclear if the same dilution effect undermines strain-mediated coupling to material defect centers. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a tensioned diamond nanobeam platform that enables enhanced strain coupling to SiV- orbital states. Through monitoring the optical response of the SiVs to the static and dynamical strain of the mechanical resonator, we observe that dynamical strain localizes near the clamps of these resonators under static strain. This allows us to enhance SiV-mechanical coupling and the mechanical coherence simultaneously, and provide a SiV-strain sensitivity with greatly improved accuracy over previous literature values. Thus, our work opens a pathway towards seconds-long coherence hybrid quantum systems utilizing point defects in diamond nanomechanics for quantum information processing.

items.title: Polarization-locked chiral persistent spin textures in two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites
items.summary: Chiral spacer cations crystallize two-dimensional hybrid perovskites in the polar Sohncke group $P2_1$, which places the polar axis in the inorganic layer. We analyze the spin-orbit field that this geometry allows and test it against first-principles spin textures of ten polar chiral lead-halide perovskites, their mirror enantiomers and four halide-substituted analogues. The point group $C_2$ with the twofold axis in the layer forbids the helical Rashba field and allows a linear term $γ_1 k_x σ_z$, the Rashba interaction of the in-plane polar axis, together with chirality-related Dresselhaus and radial terms. Thirty-four two-band $k \cdot p$ models were fitted to each band pair and ranked by the agreement of their spin directions with the calculation rather than by the band energies, which cannot distinguish them. In all strongly polar compounds, the conduction band is described by the persistent term alone, with $γ_1 = 1.09$-$1.98$ eV Å and a spin agreement of at least 0.98, whereas the best Rashba or Dresselhaus model reaches 0.20. The $R$ and $S$ enantiomers of each compound have opposite polarizations, and therefore opposite $γ_1$ and opposite persistent spin textures of equal magnitude, as required by the mirror that relates them; this holds in all ten compounds, so the choice of the enantiomer selects the spin direction. The magnitude of $γ_1$ correlates with the disparity of the in-plane Pb-X-Pb angles ($r = 0.95$). With electron masses of $0.26$-$0.43\,m_e$ along the spin-splitting directions, the associated persistent spin helices have wavelengths of 3.4-8.2 nm.

items.title: Point-Group Equivariant Neural Networks for Local Dynamics in Lattice Systems
items.summary: We develop point-group equivariant neural networks for learning local mappings used in dynamical simulations of lattice systems. The same network acts on a finite neighborhood around each site, respecting lattice translations through shared parameters. The local configuration is decomposed into features that transform according to irreducible representations of the point group, and hidden features retain this organization throughout the network. Equivariant linear maps and symmetry-allowed tensor products then learn nonlinear spatial correlations while preserving the required transformation laws. This approach avoids constructing a fixed set of hand-crafted invariant descriptors, whose selection requires choices about which local correlations to retain. It also allows the complexity of the learned mapping to grow without enlarging its spatial cutoff. We demonstrate the construction by learning the forces governing adiabatic dynamics in the square-lattice Holstein model. Comparisons with exact diagonalization test the accuracy of the predicted forces and the evolution of spatial correlations. Force evaluation scales linearly with system size, allowing the trained model to simulate charge-density-wave ordering on large lattices. These simulations reproduce anomalously slow coarsening of the charge-density-wave domains, illustrating the use of the learned local mapping for collective dynamics.

items.title: Colossal magnetoresistance in narrow-gap magnetic semiconductor Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$
items.summary: Discovering antiferromagnetic materials with a sizable colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) effect and precisely tuning their responses remain significant challenges in materials science. This work reports the synthesis, phase transitions, and magnetotransport properties of the narrow-gap Zintl arsenide Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$. The compound undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering at $T_\mathrm{N} = 9$ K and exhibits semiconducting behavior with a low-temperature activation energy of 3.2 meV, achieving a large CMR effect of $-10^4\%$ at 9 T. Below $T_\mathrm{N}$, a distinct butterfly-shaped magnetoresistance hysteresis emerges without any macroscopic ferromagnetic order, revealing a transport anomaly likely dictated by AFM domain dynamics and/or the formation and percolation of localized magnetic polarons. Furthermore, a systematic survey of reported Eu-based Zintl phases uncovers a nearly exponential scaling trend between the maximum CMR magnitude and the low-temperature activation energy. This correlation demonstrates that bandgap engineering serves as an effective strategy for tailoring magnetotransport, establishing Eu-containing Zintl phases as a versatile platform for exploring and manipulating CMR effects.

items.title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
items.summary: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that lone-pair stereoactivity, not chalcogen mass, governs both properties. Path-integral molecular dynamics shows that the volumetric thermal expansion coefficient at 300 K decreases from 8.14 x 10^-5 K^-1 in Bi2O2S to 6.72 x 10^-5 and 6.61 x 10^-5 K^-1 in Bi2O2Se and Bi2O2Te, respectively, despite a 13% larger unit cell in the telluride, whereas substituting the S mass into Bi2O2Se changes its value by only 0.6%. Lone-pair-driven Bi off-centering in orthorhombic Bi2O2S makes b-axis expansion 1.63 times a-axis expansion yet leaves in-plane thermal conduction isotropic within 3%. Phonon transport calculations including four-phonon scattering and Wigner coherence predict a thermal conductivity maximum in Bi2O2Se (1.83 and 0.95 W m^-1 K^-1 in the in-plane and cross-plane directions, respectively, at 300 K) because Bi2O2S is limited by anharmonic scattering and Bi2O2Te by slow cross-plane phonons. Thermoreflectance measurements from 300 to 500 K and in situ X-ray diffraction on Bi2O2Se single crystals agree with these predictions within 6.4%. Phonon Boltzmann transport simulations of 12-nm-wide fins, which run hotter than Fourier diffusion predicts, show that Bi2O2Se minimizes the hotspot temperature and the thermal-mismatch strain at the gate dielectric.

items.title: Nodal magnon spin current at an antiferromagnet/altermagnet junction
items.summary: We investigate the thermally driven magnon spin current across a junction between a $d$-wave altermagnet (AM) and a ferromagnet (FM) or an antiferromagnet (AFM). The current consists of a component independent of the interface angle and an angularly dependent component with the $d$-wave form. For a sublattice-symmetric interface, the two junctions behave oppositely under reversal of the altermagnetic domain: in the FM/AM junction the angularly dependent component is odd and cancels on averaging over the domains, whereas in the AFM/AM junction the angularly independent component vanishes by symmetry and the angularly dependent component survives the domain average at a fixed Néel vector of the AFM. Both follow from a selective tunneling: a pair of spins bonded across the interface transmits magnons when the spins are parallel and not when antiparallel, which makes the AFM/AM junction a magnon valve: the configuration in which the bonded spins are antiparallel blocks the current up to the sublattice admixture of the magnons. The anisotropic tunneling is detectable as the sign reversal of the current between the interfaces normal to $[310]$ and $[130]$, and the valve reads the Néel vector of the altermagnet relative to that of the antiferromagnet through the magnitude of the current at a fixed interface.

items.title: Theory of High-Temperature Fractional Chern Phases in Monolayer van der Waals Kagome Materials A$_2$T$_3$X$_4$
items.summary: Fractional Chern insulators bring the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its anyonic excitations, to zero magnetic field. So far they have been realized in moiré materials, where the long superlattice period weakens electronic interactions and confines these phases to cryogenic temperatures. Early proposals instead envisioned topological flat bands on atomic-scale lattices, where fractionalization could persist to far higher temperatures, but a suitable material has been lacking. Here we theoretically identify monolayers of the van der Waals kagome family $\mathrm{A}_2\mathrm{T}_3\mathrm{X}_4$ as such a platform, combining intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions with gate-tunable carrier density and layer assembly. Exact diagonalization of models derived from density functional theory reveals ferromagnetism over broad filling ranges, supporting diverse fractional Chern insulators, anomalous composite Fermi liquids, and charge-ordered phases. In particular, in $\mathrm{Cs}_2\mathrm{Pd}_3\mathrm{S}_4$, the fractional Chern insulator exhibits a many-body gap of approximately 26 meV in the largest system accessible with band mixing allowing at most one interband electron-hole excitation. Layer assembly further provides a natural route to fractional quantum spin Hall insulators: bilayers with antiparallel magnetizations support this phase at realistic separations. These results identify an experimentally accessible material family in which chemical composition, carrier density, and stacking offer complementary routes to fractionalization at enhanced energy scales and control over topological order.

items.title: Local Josephson response near nonmagnetic impurities and vortices in a two-orbital $s_{\pm}$ superconductor
items.summary: We study the local Josephson response near nonmagnetic impurities and vortices in a self-consistent two-orbital $s_{\pm}$ superconductor. For a local $s$-wave tip that couples equally to the two orbitals, anomalous spectral contributions of opposite sign nearly cancel in the clean sample. Nonmagnetic impurities redistribute these contributions and can reverse the local coupling without a corresponding $π$ phase shift of the bond pair fields. Negative coupling appears at off-center sites at weaker impurity potentials than at the impurity site. The impurity-induced change is concentrated at lower quasiparticle energies, while states over a broader energy range contribute to the total clean and impurity couplings. In zero field, the coupling also changes sign as the tip gap is varied, and increasing the tunneling strength can reverse the $m=1$ sine component of the current without changing the sample state. At the chosen coherence-peak energy, increasing impurity strength mainly changes the relative intensities of existing quasiparticle-interference features. In a self-consistent two-vortex state, the Josephson response develops a spatially varying phase relative to the condensate. The response and condensate share the winding close to each core, while larger loops enclose additional winding of the Josephson response. The local Josephson sign and phase reflect the anomalous spectrum and the tip--sample coupling.

items.title: Berry curvature dipole circuit quantum electrodynamics
items.summary: Quantum three-wave mixing is an important resource in superconducting quantum circuits. The traditional implementation uses Josephson junction arrays and is activated by magnetic flux. Here we introduce the Berry curvature dipole (BCD) quantum circuit element, which achieves quantum three-wave mixing without breaking time-reversal symmetry. This quantum three-wave mixing results from the BCD nonlinear Hall effect in noncentrosymmetric quantum materials taken to a dissipationless, quantum coherent few-photon regime. We show how nonlinear Hall materials can be integrated to superconducting microwave circuits to accomplish multiphoton vacuum Rabi splittings and dynamical stabilization of bosonic Schrödinger cat states. Such BCD circuit quantum electrodynamics are a concrete exemplar of a physical resource for quantum information processing enabled by nonlinear response in quantum materials.

items.title: Resonance and Transition-Channel Competition in Cavity-Assisted Floquet-State Stabilization
items.summary: Static coupling to a dissipative cavity has been proposed as a route to autonomously stabilize Floquet eigenstates. The cavity provides an energy-selective relaxation channel: when its photon energy matches a quasienergy difference modulo drive quanta, it mediates transitions between Floquet states, followed by irreversible photon loss. Here, we show that at intermediate driving frequencies, this resonance condition alone is not sufficient for stabilization. Instead, the steady state is controlled by the interplay between resonance selection and the cavity-induced transition strengths between Floquet states, which can either cooperate or compete. This interplay leads to successful stabilization, mixed steady states despite resonance, and complete breakdown near Floquet-zone hybridization. We further show that the same mechanism extends to multilevel spin-S systems, providing a general framework for understanding when static dissipation can reliably stabilize driven quantum states.

items.title: Shape dependence of Edelstein and magnetoelectric effects in the V-shaped model
items.summary: We theoretically investigate the shape dependence and microscopic mechanism of the magnetoelectric (ME) effect, including both nonmagnetic (Edelstein-type) and magnetic origins, in a V-shaped one-dimensional chain model. Numerical calculations based on the Kubo formula reveal that the nonmagnetic-driven ME response is maximized at an apex angle of $θ\approx 0.6π$. To clarify its origin, we derive a low-energy effective Hamiltonian in the $s$-orbital subspace and demonstrate that the polarity induced by the V-shaped geometry manifests as an effective spin--orbit interaction. An analytical derivation of the Green's function shows that the geometric effect can be described as a $T$-matrix contribution associated with local symmetry breaking. This scattering-theoretical representation enables us to identify the contributions of local geometric symmetry breaking to the ME response. Using a multipole-basis representation, we identify symmetry-based selection rules for the ME tensor and show that the coupling between the effective spin--orbit interaction and the orbital angular momentum generated across the apex plays an essential role. The resulting angular dependence, $\sinθ\sin{θ/2}$, peaks at $θ= 2\tan^{-1}\sqrt{2} \approx 0.608π$, in good agreement with the numerical results. We also analyze a ferromagnetic V-shaped model including the Zeeman interaction and show that the magnetic-driven ME response originates from the spin magnetization induced by the coupling between the electric-field--driven charge-potential gradient and the Zeeman term. These results reveal distinct ME mechanisms depending on the presence or absence of time-reversal symmetry and clarify the microscopic origin of shape-dependent ME responses in V-shaped chains.

items.title: Algorithmic Locality of Quantum Tensor Network Belief Propagation
items.summary: Belief propagation has recently emerged as a powerful framework for evaluating tensor networks in higher dimensions, combining computational efficiency with provable analytical guarantees. In this work, we develop the first end-to-end theory of tensor network belief propagation for a class of projected entangled pair states satisfying \emph{strong injectivity}. We show that when the injectivity parameter exceeds a constant threshold, BP fixed points can be found efficiently, and a cluster-corrected BP algorithm computes physical quantities to $1/\mathrm{poly}(N)$ error in $\mathrm{poly}(N)$ time for an $N$ qubit system. We further identify a striking phenomenon we term \emph{algorithmic locality}: local perturbations of the tensor network affect the BP fixed point with an influence decaying rapidly with distance. Moreover, through the cluster expansion, this locality extends to observables, implying that local expectation values can be approximated from local data with controlled accuracy. We exhibit three regimes admitting strong injectivity: random Gaussian PEPS with large physical dimension, high-temperature Gibbs states of commuting two-body Hamiltonians, and fixed-depth quantum circuits subject to sufficiently strong depolarizing noise. Our bounds are worst-case sufficient conditions and do not identify sharp algorithmic transitions.

items.title: Mechanistic discovery in grain boundary structure and deformation driven by agentic AI
items.summary: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending these capabilities to domain-intensive mechanistic studies remains challenging. General grain boundaries (GBs) exemplify this challenge, as their structural complexity complicates experimental characterization and atomistic modeling. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general GBs, which are common in real polycrystals yet remain understudied. By integrating large language models into a modular architecture, GBClaw effectively combines systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis through iterative workflow refinement and dynamic replanning. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, the framework characterized interfacial defect structures and deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. It established a general approach to identify previously unobserved, widely spaced secondary GB misfit dislocations (SGBMDs) alongside closely spaced primary GB misfit dislocations (PGBMDs) in simulated atomic configurations and experimental images. Comparisons of GB sliding with and without SGBMDs revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of misfit-dislocation hierarchies in sliding resistance. Researcher-guided follow-up calculations further elucidated the structural origins of shear asymmetry and an anomalous shear response. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening and deep mechanistic discovery at complex material interfaces.

items.title: Atomic Charge Chirality from Electric Multipoles
items.summary: We establish an electric-multipole ($Q_{lm}$) criterion for chirality of local atomic charge distributions. For the 11 crystallographic chiral point groups, we identify representative lowest-rank multipole contents required to distinguish the opposite handednesses. For the axial groups $C_n$ and $D_n$ with $n=2,3,4,6$, chirality arises from the relative orientation of two azimuthal anisotropies with $m=n$, belonging to consecutive ranks $l=n$ and $n+1$. Their coexistence produces a latitude-dependent twist of the $n$-fold charge distribution. The polar component, although allowed in $C_n$, is distinct from this chiral mechanism and is not required for handedness. The cubic groups $T$ and $O$ exhibit distinct realizations, with octahedral chirality first appearing at rank nine. We further show that, within a spinless $s$-$p$-$d$-$f$ atomic basis, the scalar charge density contains multipoles only up to rank six and therefore cannot encode the handedness of $C_6$, $D_6$, or $O$. These results connect electric-multipole content and atomic orbital degrees of freedom to the microscopic encoding of crystallographic handedness.

items.title: The Constructive Cavity Method for the Ising Perceptron
items.summary: We apply the Constructive Cavity Method (CCM) to the Ising perceptron. The process starts from positive soft channels admitting an auxiliary representation $$ U(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{tx}ρ(\mathrm{d}t),\qquad ρ\ge0, $$ with an auxiliary measure having a finite exponential quadratic moment. This rewrites the perceptron as a dense, bipartite Gaussian model with an Ising layer and a continuous auxiliary layer. The CCM blanket geometry then gives two constructive variance profiles, $Q_\ell$ on the Ising side and $Γ_\ell$ on the auxiliary side. The bipartite shell scale is $$ Q_{\ell+1}Γ_{\ell+1}-Q_\ellΓ_\ell, $$ and Gaussian core comparison removes the core contribution $ΔQ_\ellΔΓ_\ell$ under blanket refinement. The scalar cavity functional has three terms, $$ \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{perc}}(ν)=\mathbb{E}\left[\log\langle2\cosh x\rangle_ν+α\log\langle U(s)\rangle_ν-\log\langle e^y\rangle_ν\right], $$ where $x$ is the new-spin field, $s$ is the new-constraint field, and $y$ is the cavity correction. CCM identifies the constructive cavity variables with the Aizenman--Sims--Starr random overlap structure (ROSt) variables. Parisi's recursive averaging then gives $$ \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{perc}}^{\mathrm{CCM}}(ζ,Q,Γ)=X_0(0)+αY_0(0)-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\ell=0}^{R}ζ_\ell\left(Q_{\ell+1}Γ_{\ell+1}-Q_\ellΓ_\ell\right). $$ The replica-symmetric specialization gives Gardner's formula for the generalized Ising perceptron. Specializing the constraint terminal to the hard channel gives the Krauth--Mézard functional for the binary perceptron.

items.title: An Instability of the Quantum Markov Length
items.summary: The Markov length, the length scale governing the exponential decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) in a quantum many-body state, has proven useful for characterizing mixed-state phases of matter. Nevertheless, we show that a state's Markov length is not generally stable under weak local channels. The failure of stability occurs already at a pure product state. We demonstrate this explicitly in a one-dimensional fermionic chain, where a fine-tuned depth-two circuit of nearest-neighbor Gaussian channels maps the vacuum to a state whose CMI decays \emph{algebraically} and whose Markov length is therefore infinite, even when the channels are taken arbitrarily close to the identity. The algebraic decay is rooted in the nonanalyticity of the von Neumann entropy at rank-deficient density operators. We exhibit an analogous instability on an ordinary qubit chain. More generally, we show that the Markov length is unstable in any translation-invariant state with even a single rank-deficient reduced density operator. These results pose a challenge to recent definitions of mixed-state phase equivalence based on the Markov length.

items.title: Two faces of symmetry match in gear-like coupled rotary motors
items.summary: Rotary molecular motors commonly couple components with different rotational symmetries, but how this gearing controls energy transduction remains unclear. Here we show that symmetry can produce a fundamental tradeoff in coupled stochastic barrierless rotary motors: the gear ratio that maximizes output power under tight coupling is also the ratio that requires the strongest coupling to remain locked. Consequently, weakening the coupling can invert the effect of gearing, transforming a power maximum into a local minimum. At strong driving, both the power-optimal and most slip-susceptible ratios approach symmetry match. Numerical solutions of the Fokker-Planck dynamics for rotors with finite energy barriers reproduce these predictions and reveal how the behavior changes when driving strength is fixed per rotation or per subunit. Motivated by the bacterial flagellar motor, these results identify coupling strength as a key determinant of whether matched rotational symmetries enhance or suppress energy transduction, providing a general design principle for coupled molecular motors.

items.title: Pole Skipping, Avoided Crossing, and Resonant Excitation in Kerr Quasinormal Modes near Algebraically Special Frequencies
items.summary: Kerr quasinormal modes near algebraically special frequencies exhibit anomalous behavior, including apparent bifurcation, disappearance, and a nonsmooth connection to the Schwarzschild limit, which has remained puzzling for decades. Tracking poles and zeros of Green-function building blocks across different Riemann sheets, we show that the bifurcation is due to an avoided crossing accompanied by resonant excitation, while the disappearance is due to pole skipping caused by cancellation of a quasinormal-mode pole by a Matsubara-mode zero. This resolves the physical origin of these long-standing anomalies.

items.title: Transcendental momentum quantization in Rashba nanowires and zero energy states in their normal and superconducting phase
authors: Nico Leumer, Harald Schmid, Milena Grifoni and Magdalena Marganska
items.summary: We study finite system properties of the canonical low energy model for a semiconducting nanowire with Rashba spin–orbit coupling (SOC). The case of an isolated wire as well as of one proximitized by an s-wave superconductor are considered. Already for the normal wire, the presence of SOC leads to eigenstates of the finite system composed of more than two momentum eigenstates. The exact quantization condition for the wavevectors is not that of a quantum box, but given instead by a transcendental equation linking the involved wavevectors. For the wire with superconducting pairing, the presence of electron and hole channels complicates the composition of the eigenstates. In this case we derive an approximate quantization condition close to the phase boundary, and an approximate condition for the appearance of exact zero energy states. It can be satisfied both in the topological and in the trivial phase. Both the trivial and topological zero energy states contribute to the linear transport through Andreev reflection and direct transmission processes, with their relative importance depending on the degree of the states’ localization at the boundary. A negative spin-flip interference contribution causes trivial zero-energy states to exhibit a zero-bias conductance plateau, whereas Majorana zero modes (MZM) display a peak. This distinct lineshape may serve as an experimental signature for the identification of MZM and to discriminate the topological phases.

items.title: Zak phase and bulk-boundary correspondence in a generalized Dirac–Kronig–Penney model
authors: Giuliano Angelone, Domenico Monaco and Gabriele Peluso
items.summary: We investigate the topological properties of a generalized Dirac–Kronig–Penney model, a continuum one-dimensional model for a relativistic quantum chain. By tuning the coupling parameters this model can accommodate five Altland–Zirnbauer–Cartan symmetry classes, three of which (AIII, BDI and D) support non-trivial topological phases in dimension one. We characterize analytically the spectral properties of the Hamiltonian in terms of a spectral function, and numerically compute the Zak phase to probe the bulk topological content of the insulating phases. Our findings reveal that, while the Zak phase is quantized in classes AIII and BDI, it exhibits non-quantized values in class D, challenging its traditional role as a topological marker in continuum settings. We also discuss the bulk-boundary correspondence for a truncated version of the chain, analyzing how the emergence of edge states depends on both the truncation position and the boundary conditions. In classes AIII and BDI, we find that the Zak phase effectively detects edge states as a relative boundary topological index, although the correspondence is highly sensitive to the parameters characterizing the truncation.

items.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
The Roaming Bethe Roots: An Effective Bethe Ansatz Beyond Integrability
authors: Wenlong Zhao, 文龙 赵, Yunfeng Jiang, 云峰 江, Rui-Dong Zhu and 睿东 朱
items.summary: We propose an effective Bethe ansatz (EBA) for solving quantum many-body systems near an integrable point. Our approach retains the functional form of the Bethe wave function while renormalizing the Bethe roots to account for integrability-breaking interactions. These effective roots are determined by minimizing physically motivated cost functions. The resulting off-shell Bethe states serve as approximate eigenstates of the non-integrable models. We assess the quality of the approximation using various physical observables, including the energy eigenvalue, state fidelity, and bipartite entanglement entropy. Our tests show that for models with weak integrability-breaking, the EBA provides a high-quality approximation to the exact eigenstates over a wide range of deformation parameters. In contrast, for models with strong integrability-breaking interactions, the efficacy of EBA degrades relatively quickly as the deformation parameter increases. The efficacy of the method thus offers a useful probe for characterizing the strength of integrability breaking. Within its regime of accuracy, it also provides a new representation of the eigenstates of nearly integrable models, enabling one to exploit the algebraic structure inherited from integrability.

items.title: Unveiling the Elusive Σ(1380) Resonance through Coupled-Channel Dynamics in Λ c + ηπ + Λ Reaction
authors: Wen-Tao Lyu, 文韬 吕, Si-Wei Liu, 思威 刘, Jia-Jun Wu, 佳俊 吴, De-Min Li, 德民 李, En Wang and 恩 王
items.summary: We investigate the Λc+ ηπ +Λ decay measured by the Belle and BESIII Collaborations, focusing on the possible role of the Σ(1380) state with spin-parity J P=1/2−. In our theoretical framework, the Λ(1670) and a0(980) are dynamically generated from meson–baryon and meson–meson final-state interactions, respectively, and the corresponding line shapes of these two states used here are applicable to all relevant hadronic reactions. Furthermore, the contributions from the intermediate Σ(1385) resonance and the possible Σ(1380) state are included explicitly. By comparing the invariant mass and angular distributions obtained with and without the Σ(1380) state, we demonstrate that this state plays an important role in improving the description of the experimental data. We also identify the kinematic regions most sensitive to the possible Σ(1380) contribution. Future high-precision measurements of this process will be instrumental for testing the existence of the Σ state with J P=1/2−.

items.title: Anomalous Local Enhancement of Thermal Conductivity under Nanoscale Hotspot: Spatial Inhomogeneity and Phonon Nonequilibrium in Silicon
authors: Yuxin Luo, 雨欣 罗, Shuai Wu, 帅 吴, Dongdong Kang, 冬冬 康, Xiaoxiang Yu, 晓翔 余, Jiayu Dai and 佳钰 戴
items.summary: The miniaturization of electronic devices gives rise to localized heat accumulation and thus nanoscale hotspots, triggering degenerated heat dissipation. However, the phonon transport mechanism and quantification of inhomogeneous nonequilibrium thermal conductivity remain elusive. Here, through molecular dynamics simulations of silicon thin film under nanoscale hotspot, we reveal a dramatic spatial inhomogeneity of cross-plane thermal conductivity κz under nanoscale hotspot excitation. Contrary to the conventional picture of phonon nonequilibrium simply suppressing heat transport, we find a non-monotonic spatial evolution: κz drops by up to 68% immediately beneath the hotspot (Lhot=10.9 nm), but subsequently recovers to exceed the uniform-heating baseline by 12% at a distance of ~40 nm, producing a maximum κz gradient of 3.2 W·m−1·K−1·nm−1—2.3 times that of uniform heating. Spectral decomposition indicates that longitudinal acoustic (LA) phonons dominate the anomalous local thermal conductivity enhancement. Modal temperature calculations reveal that the spatial relaxation of hotspot-induced LA phonon nonequilibrium matches well with the transition of thermal conductivity from suppression to anomalous enhancement. The magnitude of the spatial inhomogeneity diminishes with rising temperature (from 3.05 W·m−1·K−1·nm−1 at 300 K to 1.25 W·m−1·K−1·nm−1 at 600 K) due to increased anharmonic scattering. These findings challenge the common assumption of spatially uniform thermal conductivity in hotspot systems and provide a quantitative, spectrally resolved benchmark for thermal management of nanoscale devices.

items.title: Tunable Insulator–Metal Transitions and Flat Bands in Domain-Wall-Engineered Monolayer In2Se3
authors: Laiyuan Su, 来源 苏, Zhigang Gui, 志刚 桂, Li Huang and 丽 黄
items.summary: Ferroelectric domain walls (DWs) provide a promising platform for dynamically tuning electronic properties at the nanoscale. Using first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that charged DWs in monolayer α-In2Se3 enable versatile band engineering across one and two dimensions. In one-dimensional DW arrays, the separation between tail-to-tail and head-to-head DWs controls the band gap: with increasing inter-wall distance, the valence and conduction bands, dominated respectively by the oppositely charged DWs, shift in opposite directions under contrasting local electrostatic potentials, leading to continuous gap reduction and ultimately an insulator-to-metal transition. Extending to two dimensions, periodic DW networks form a breathing kagome lattice, wherein each DW segment acts as a “super-atom”, yielding nearly dispersionless flat bands near the Fermi level. In addition, an isolated conduction band originating from the P↓ domains emerges near the Fermi level, with decreasing bandwidth as the superlattice size increases, giving rise to an effective triangular lattice. Our findings establish DW-engineered In2Se3 as a reconfigurable platform that bridges ferroelectric switching with quantum materials design, offering a promising route toward a possible platform for exploring emergent quantum phenomena in artificially engineered lattices.

items.title: A polymer-embedded molecular fuse for safer high-nickel lithium batteries
items.summary: Abstract Thermal runaway in high-energy lithium batteries is driven by autocatalytic radical reactions and flammable gas accumulation, posing a critical safety bottleneck for next-generation energy storage. Here we report a cathode-integrated polymeric molecular fuse enabling thermally responsive safety control without compromising electrochemical performance. By tuning inductive and hyperconjugative effects of phosphonate side chains, the dissociation energy of sacrificial P–C bonds is regulated, yielding an ∼10°C shift in activation temperature, as supported by density functional theory and in situ variable-temperature Raman spectroscopy. Upon activation, P-centered radicals suppress exothermic chain reactions, achieving a 76% reduction in heat release and delaying thermal runaway in LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathodes and 0.6 Ah Li-metal pouch cells. Notably, the activation threshold exceeds typical cathode processing temperatures, preventing premature radical generation during fabrication while enabling on-demand safety activation. This work establishes a substituent-regulated molecular fuse that couples fabrication-compatible stability with triggerable intrinsic safety, transforming battery thermal management from passive suppression to controllable molecular-level reaction pathways.

items.title: Incoherent diffraction imaging with a pseudo-thermal light source
authors: Pablo San Miguel Claveria, Peer Biesterfeld, Sebastião Antunes, Matilde Fernandes, Matilde Garcia, Matilde Nunes, Lucas Ansia Fernandez, Gareth O Williams, Sven Froehlich, David Theidel, Philip Mosel, Ihsan Fsaifes, Andrea Trabattoni, Marco Piccardo, Jean-Christophe Chanteloup, Milutin Kovacev, Hamed Merdji and Marta Fajardo
items.summary: Incoherent diffraction imaging—IDI—is a lensless imaging technique that has been recently proposed to exploit the partial coherence of incoherently scattered light to retrieve structural information from the scattering centers. Similar to the stellar intensity interferometry of Hanbury Brown and Twiss, the signal builds up on the second-order spatial correlations of the emitted light. The complex spatial distribution of the target is thereby encoded in the spatial intensity fluctuations of the scattered light. The first experimental realizations of this imaging technique have been realized using the fluorescence excited by an ultra-short x-ray pulse at free electron laser (FEL) facilities. Here, we propose an alternative setup based on a table-top pseudo-thermal light source that works as an optical emulator of the FEL experiment. This setup allows us to explore IDI under a wide range of physically relevant conditions as well as to benchmark numerical and analytical models currently used to determine the imaging capabilities of this technique.

items.title: Requirements for teleportation in an intercity quantum network
authors: Soubhadra Maiti, Guus Avis, Sounak Kar and Stephanie Wehner
items.summary: We investigate the hardware requirements for quantum teleportation in an intercity-scale network topology consisting of two metropolitan-scale networks connected via a long-distance backbone link. Specifically, we identify the minimal improvements required beyond the state-of-the-art to achieve an end-to-end expected teleportation fidelity of , which represents the classical limit. To this end, we formulate the hardware requirements computation as optimisation problems, where the hardware parameters representing the underlying device capabilities serve as decision variables. Assuming a simplified noise model, we derive closed-form analytical expressions for the teleportation fidelity and rate when the network is realised using heterogeneous quantum hardware, including a quantum repeater chain with a memory cut-off. Our derivations are based on events defined by the order statistics of link generation durations in both the metropolitan networks and the backbone, and the resulting expressions are verified against NetSquid simulations. The analytical expressions facilitate efficient exploration of the optimisation parameter space without resorting to computationally intensive simulations. We then apply this framework to a representative realisation in which the metropolitan nodes are based on trapped-ion processors and the backbone is composed of ensemble-based quantum memories. Our results suggest that teleportation across metropolitan distances already reaches the classical limit with state-of-the-art hardware when the data qubit is prepared after end-to-end entanglement has been established, whereas extending teleportation to intercity scales requires additional, though plausibly achievable, improvements in hardware performance.

items.title: Finite quantum pumps for phase-locked parametric amplification: requirements for quantum-battery work sources
items.summary: Quantum batteries have been proposed as locally precharged work sources for superconducting quantum technologies, suggesting a route to reduce continuously supplied microwave drives. Here we ask what a finite bosonic pump must provide to replace the pump tone of a nondegenerate parametric amplifier during a readout window. Quantizing the pump exposes a resource distinction hidden in the classical description: stored energy and the ordinary marginal signal response can survive pump phase twirling, whereas a reproducible phase-locked signal-idler field requires pump coherences in the number sectors coupled by the mixing process. In a closed trilinear model, a coherent pump and its number-matched phase-twirled counterpart generate the same number-like marginal observables, but only the coherent pump produces anomalous two-mode coherence and an EPR-squeezed interference dip. Including leakage, we collect the emitted fields into cascaded temporal modes. At matched collector bandwidth, the coherent pump gives the interference certifier , whereas the phase-randomized control gives . A weak seeded-signal analysis shows more sharply that an exact pump phase twirl leaves the collected signal marginal invariant by phase covariance while eliminating the anomalous signal-idler coherence. A finite-cutoff scan also indicates that weak amplitude squeezing can modestly deepen the phase-sensitive dip by reducing pump-number fluctuations while preserving most of the coherent displacement. Thus, for the three-wave-mixing pump families studied here, adjacent-number pump coherence is the resource that establishes a phase-locked joint amplifier field, rather than a prerequisite for energy transfer or ordinary marginal signal response.

items.summary: The motion of active particles is usually fixed by their microscopic design. Zhang et al. show that short active molecules with intramolecular nonreciprocal coupling can instead be programmed through their internal sequence. Different sequences generate persistent, circling, or wriggling motion and alter how long molecules retain their direction of motion. For three-particle molecules, different internal sequences shift the onset of motility-induced phase separation by more than three orders of magnitude, linking single-molecule dynamics to collective organization.

items.title: A comprehensive benchmark of an Ising machine on the Max-Cut problem
authors: Salwa Shaglel, Markus Kirsch, Marten Winkler, Christian Münch, Stefan Walter, Fritz Schinkel and Martin Kliesch
items.summary: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) formulations of combinatorial optimization problems allow for solving them using various quantum heuristics. While large-scale quantum computations are currently still out of reach, we can already numerically test such QUBO formulations on a perhaps surprisingly large scale. In this work, we benchmark Fujitsu’s Digital Annealer (DA) on the Max-Cut problem, which captures the main complexity of the QUBO problem. We make a comprehensive benchmark against leading other heuristic algorithms on graphs with up to 53,000 variables by focusing on the wall-clock time. Moreover, we compare the DA performance against published performance results of the D-Wave hybrid quantum–classical annealer and the recently proposed QIS3 heuristic. Based on performance statistics for over 2000 graphs from the MQLib, we find that the DA yields competitive results. We hope that this benchmark demonstrates the extent to which large QUBO instances can be heuristically solved today, yielding consistent results across different solvers.

items.title: A field-quadrature perspective on strong-field ionization with squeezed light
authors: Haoyu Liu, Jianmin Yuan and Xu Wang
items.summary: Bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) has emerged as a macroscopic nonclassical light source capable of driving strong-field processes. Yet its broad, long-tailed photon-number distribution bears little resemblance to the narrow poissonian distribution of a coherent field, obscuring how the corresponding strong-field responses are connected. We show that field-quadrature space supplies the missing continuous description: coherent, squeezed coherent, and BSV states are Gaussian wave packets distinguished only by their centers and widths. This representation provides a unified framework for tracing the coherent-to-BSV transition at fixed mean photon number and for analyzing both ionization yields and photoelectron spectra. Crucially, BSV is a symmetry-protected endpoint in quadrature space. Near the BSV limit, we identify a simple scaling law of the ionization response associated with a residual coherent component. We show that this scaling arises from parity-induced stationarity with respect to the Gaussian center, together with the accompanying width variation near the BSV limit. The result provides a symmetry-based criterion for approaching the BSV regime and a potential probe of a mode-matched coherent displacement through the strong-field response itself.

items.title: Exact Finite Response of Higher-Order Statistics in Nonequilibrium Networks
authors: Ruicheng Bao, Shiling Liang and 师翎 梁
items.summary: We develop an exact finite-perturbation response theory for the higher-order statistics of general state observables in nonequilibrium Markov networks. For local perturbations, the moment generating function obeys an exact nonlinear response identity in the perturbation strength, controlled by a single kinetic parameter α. This induces an exact nonlinear map for the cumulant generating function and closed expressions for finite responses of all cumulants through partial Bell polynomials. As a central application, we obtain a complete theory of variance control, including sharp saturation limits, a classification of monotone-suppression and sign-reversal regimes, and mean-first-passage-time design principles for optimal noise suppression. The same framework yields exact formulas for operational and symmetrized response resolution along the accessible control branch. A four-state gene-regulation model illustrates how local kinetic control suppresses the occupancy noise of a transcriptionally competent promoter state.

items.title: A Collision-State Criterion for Two-Peak Collisions in a Two-Dimensional Long-Wave–Short-Wave Resonance Interaction System
authors: Wei Dong, 伟 董, Houhui Yi, 厚会 伊, Xiaofeng Li, 晓凤 李, Muwei Liu, 慕威 刘, Zhiyang Zhang and 之阳 张
items.summary: This Letter investigates the finite-time morphology of two-pulse collisions in a two-dimensional long-wave–short-wave resonance interaction system with a local cubic perturbation. An integral identity for the centered second moment separates the collision dynamics into contributions from dispersive spreading, local quartic overlap, and long-wave feedback. For the prescribed two-sech initial-data family and the finite observation interval T ≤ 7, these contributions distinguish double-peak and single-peak morphologies with an accuracy of 94.17%. A feedforward neural network is then employed to efficiently reconstruct the distribution of the identity-based result in the parameter plane of the nonintegrable coefficient and relative phase. This distribution shows that variation of the relative phase can change the collision morphology.

items.title: NextCrystal: A Symmetry-Driven Generative Framework for Crystal Structure Prediction
authors: Jinming Mu, 锦铭 穆, Lixin He, 力新 何, Xudong Zhu, 旭东 朱, Shi Yin and 实 殷
items.summary: Crystal structure prediction (CSP), which aims to predict the 3D atomic arrangement of a crystal from its composition, is central to materials discovery and mechanistic understanding. Crystal symmetry plays a crucial role in CSP, but given the composition in a unit cell, existing methods either struggle with the NP-hard combinatorial challenge of enforcing symmetry rigorously or rely on retrieving known templates, inherently limiting both physical fidelity and the discovery of genuinely new materials. To address this challenge, we introduce NextCrystal, a symmetry-driven generative framework that employs language models to encode chemical semantics and directly generate fine-grained Wyckoff site patterns from atomic stoichiometry, without retrieving pre-existing structural templates at inference. To overcome the combinatorial complexity of site assignments, we incorporate domain knowledge via an efficient, linear-complexity heuristic beam search, rigorously enforcing algebraic consistency between site multiplicities and atomic stoichiometry. By integrating this symmetry-consistent template into a diffusion backbone, the framework constrains the stochastic generative trajectory to a physically plausible geometric manifold. NextCrystal achieves state-of-the-art performance on stability, uniqueness, and novelty benchmarks, as well as superior structural matching, establishing a paradigm for exploring previously unexplored crystallographic space without relying on prior structural templates. As a blind-rediscovery case study, NextCrystal recovers the known low-energy antipolar oV Pnma polymorph of HfO2, which is absent from the training dataset, without retrieving a structural prototype during inference. Standardized structure matching after a common first-principles relaxation confirms its equivalence to the published oV/a62 structure and its distinction from the conventional high-pressure cotunnite/oII Pnma phase.

items.title: Thermal Signatures of the Slater–Mott Crossover in the Hubbard Model: From Double Occupancy to Antiferromagnetic Correlation Length
authors: Mingzhong Lu, 明忠 卢, Yu-Feng Song, 育峰 宋, Youjin Deng, 友金 邓, Yuan-Yao He and 院耀 何
items.summary: The interaction-driven crossover from a Slater insulator to a Mott insulator in the Néel-ordered ground state of the Hubbard model is a fundamental paradigm of strongly correlated electrons, yet its quantitative characterization has remained elusive. Here we establish a clear and experimentally accessible thermal criterion for this crossover via the sign change of the temperature derivative of double occupancy, (∂D/∂T)U, near zero temperature. In the Slater regime, (∂D/∂T)U > 0 reflects the major role of charge fluctuations; in the Mott regime, the anomalous (∂D/∂T)U < 0, a manifestation of the Pomeranchuk effect, signals the dominance of low-energy spin superexchange physics. Using exact diagonalization and numerically exact quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that this criterion determines the crossover boundary at Ucross/t = 4.0(2) for the half-filled two-dimensional Hubbard model. Furthermore, we obtain a consistent boundary independently from the maximum in the antiferromagnetic correlation length, which also arises from the superexchange physics. These two thermal signatures are theoretically unified through the local minimum of thermal entropy versus interaction U at low temperatures. Our results offer a direct, measurable, and physically intuitive framework to identify the SlaterMott crossover in optical lattice experiments.

items.summary: An XOR-FWHT algorithm is presented for the deterministic evaluation of the second-order stabilizer Rényi entropy of generic N -qubit pure states represented as full state vectors, reducing the computational cost from 𝒪(8 N ) to 𝒪( N 4 N ). The method exploits XOR-shifted amplitude correlations and fast Walsh-Hadamard transforms, without relying on sampling or special structure of the input state.

Quantitative comparison with an anisotropic spin-1/2 model places the material further from the exactly solvable quantum critical point than previously estimated, suggesting that structural disorder may contribute to the suppression of magnetic order.

items.title: Ultrathin BiO x Charge-Transfer Doping for Cross-TMD Electronic Modulation and Homogeneous WSe 2 Inverters
authors: Ching-Hao Hsu, Yu-Wei Hsu, Ta-Wei Hsu, Yu-Tung Lin, Li-Ya Chiu, I-Chih Ni, and Chih-I Wu
items.summary: Abstract Charge-transfer doping provides a nondestructive route to tune two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), but selectively patterned n-type dopants effective across different TMD channels remain limited. Here, ultrathin bismuth oxide (BiO x ) is used as an n-type charge-transfer doping and passivation layer for monolayer MoS 2 and WSe 2 transistors. In MoS 2 , 2 nm BiO x preserves the channel structure and yields a TLM-extracted effective contact resistance of 0.71 ± 0.06 kΩ·μm at n 2D = 1.8 × 10 13 cm –2 . Thicker BiO x strengthens n-type modulation but reduces gate controllability. The modulation remains stable after ambient storage and air annealing. BiO x also enhances electron transport in WSe 2 and enables homogeneous WSe 2 inverters with MoO x -doped p-FETs, achieving a gain of ∼19 and a total normalized noise margin of 0.895 V DD at V DD = 2 V. These results establish BiO x as a cross-TMD n-type charge-transfer dopant for contact, threshold-voltage, and polarity engineering.

items.title: Engineering High-Entropy Tetrahedrite Cu–Zn–Sb–Ag–Bi–S Nanocrystals via Sequential Cation Exchange as Efficient Catalysts for Hydrogen Evolution Reactions
authors: Ankita Bora, Suvodeep Sen, Niraj Nitish Patil, Temilade Esther Edgoke, Kevin M. Ryan, and Shalini Singh
items.summary: Abstract High-entropy chalcogenides represent an emerging class of functional materials with immense potential in broad applications. To date, colloidal high-entropy nanocrystals (NCs) have predominantly been accessed via co-nucleation of precursors or simultaneous incorporation of multiple cations. While effective, these approaches lack a mechanistic understanding of NC synthesis. Here, we report the colloidal synthesis of high-entropy Cu–Zn–Sb–Ag–Bi–S NCs in the tetrahedrite phase, employing a sequential, low-temperature cation-exchange strategy, starting from a Cu–Zn–Sb–S tetrahedrite template. Subsequent sequential cation exchanges preserve the crystal phase while enabling precise control over morphology. This bottom-up approach circumvents the need for high-temperature synthesis, while allowing isolation and characterization of intermediate states, providing important mechanistic insight into the evolution of high-entropy NCs. The nanocrystals served as hydrogen evolution reaction electrocatalysts with less negative cathodic potentials. This work introduces the high-entropy tetrahedrite phase, paving the way for entropy-stabilized chalcogenides for energy conversion applications.

items.title: Precursor-Free Photoelectrochemical Fabrication of Spiral Lead Oxide Nanostructures under Circularly Polarized Light
authors: Ami Hayakawa, Tetsu Tatsuma, and Hiroyasu Nishi
items.summary: Abstract Chiral nanostructures have attracted considerable attention because of their strong interactions with circularly polarized light (CPL) and their various applications. Although various fabrication methods have been reported, photoelectrochemical approaches using CPL as the chiral source are attractive because of their simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and scalability. However, previous CPL-based methods have required two or more steps, including the preparation of anisotropic precursors. Here, we demonstrate a single-step method for the selective growth of chiral PbO 2 nanostructures with handedness dictated by CPL at a chiral yield of 87%, by simply irradiating a transparent electrode with CPL, without using precursor nanoparticles. The obtained structures exhibit well-defined spiral morphologies and high chiroptical activity with maximum dissymmetry factors (g-factors) ranging from 0.006 to 0.010. This conceptual framework, involving symmetry breaking through random nucleation and Mie-resonance-mediated spiral growth under CPL, may be applicable to the template-free fabrication of various chiral nanomaterials.

items.title: Pressure Engineering through Silica Nanoconfinement for Melting Point Elevation of Gold Nanoparticles
authors: Chang-Won Choi, Jeong Hun Choi, Gi-Yeop Kim, In Su Lee, and Si-Young Choi
items.summary: Abstract Au nanoparticles (NPs) are inherently thermally unstable at elevated temperatures because their large surface-to-volume ratio promotes melting, migration, and coalescence. Here, we demonstrate that silica (SiO 2 ) nanoconfinement thermodynamically elevates the melting point ( T m ) of Au NPs through confinement-induced compressive pressure. Atomic-resolution in situ heating scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) combined with local Fourier crystallinity mapping reveals that bare Au NPs lose crystallinity at 1,000 °C, whereas SiO 2 -encapsulated Au cores (Au@SiO 2 ) remain crystalline. Accordingly, in situ heating TEM shows bare Au NPs progressively merge while Au@SiO 2 remain structurally isolated. Temperature-dependent lattice-parameter measurements reveal significantly suppressed thermal expansion of confined Au cores, corresponding to an estimated compressive stress of 4–5 GPa. Finite-element simulations support this estimate, showing that SiO 2 shell shrinkage generates several-GPa core pressure, with thicker shells producing higher pressure and greater T m elevation. These findings establish nanoconfinement-induced pressure as a general thermomechanical strategy for stabilizing metallic NPs under extreme thermal environments.

items.title: Magnetism beyond the Monolayer: Long-Range Order in an Interfacial Phase of CoBr 2
authors: Samuel Kerschbaumer, David Serrate, Adriana Elizabet Candia, Andrea Aguirre, Danilo Longo, Fadi Choueikani, Jorge Lobo-Checa, Pavel Jelínek, Maxim Ilyn, Celia Rogero, and Sebastien E. Hadjadj
items.summary: Abstract Transition metal dihalides are promising magnetic van der Waals materials because of their structural simplicity, chemical stability, and compatibility with nanofabrication. While magnetic order in these systems is typically associated with bulk-like monolayers, its relation to interfacial phases remains largely unexplored. Here we show that in CoBr 2 grown on Au(111), long-range magnetic order already emerges in a structurally distinct interfacial precursor phase, prior to the formation of the bulk-like monolayer. During growth, this phase evolves into the monolayer, accompanied by a transition from molecular-like states to semiconducting behavior. Spin-resolved STM reveals an inhomogeneous in-plane magnetic response that is locally suppressed by point defects, whereas macroscopic XMCD demonstrates robust long-range order with pronounced in-plane anisotropy. These results establish that long-range magnetic order in CoBr 2 does not require an ideal bulk-like monolayer but can emerge from interfacial phases with distinct electronic and structural properties, enabling magnetism beyond the monolayer limit.
